name: Oxford rampion
grown_as: A perennial rock-garden plant from the Alps, named for the old walls of Oxford where it grows wild. William's library gives Phyteuma scheuchzeri, which is the plant called Oxford rampion or horned rampion. Described as that.
habit: A low, tufted perennial 20 to 40 cm from a thick root, the leafy stems upright to arching.

leaf.arrangement: A tuft of basal leaves; alternate up the stem
leaf.outline: Basal leaves narrow lance-shaped (sometimes broader), 5 to 15 cm; stem leaves narrow, almost grass-like, getting smaller upwards
leaf.base: Basal leaves tapering into a long stalk; stem leaves stalkless
leaf.margin: Smooth or with small, fine, uneven teeth
leaf.stalk: Long on basal leaves; none on stem leaves

flower.form: A round ball of 15 to 30 small flowers packed together
flower.petals: Five narrow petals joined at the tip into a curved, claw-like tube in bud; later they split apart from the base into five thin strips
flower.centre: Long styles stick out of the flowers, each ending in two or three curled stigma lobes
flower.behind: Several long, narrow, leafy bracts under the head, longer than the head and spreading like horns
flower.carried: Alone at the tip of each stem, upright or nodding a little

fruit: Small dry capsules in a brownish head, the long horn-like bracts still sticking out. Seeds tiny, oval, flattened and shiny brown.
seedling: Two tiny round seed leaves. The first true leaves are oval and stalked.
winter: Dies down to the thick root; a few small leaves may stay at the base.

leaf: narrow lance-shaped leaf on a long stalk
bloom: round ball of many narrow, curved, claw-like flowers
long narrow bracts sticking out beneath the head like horns
styles with curled tips sticking out
young: low tuft of narrow, long-stalked leaves
flower: low arching leafy stems 20 to 40 cm
each stem topped by one round blue ball with horn-like bracts beneath
seedhead: brown dried head with the long bracts still sticking out
dormant: perhaps a small tuft of leaves at the base

look_alikes: Round-headed rampion (Phyteuma orbiculare), wild on southern chalk downs, has short bracts that do not stick out beyond the head. Spiked rampion (Phyteuma spicatum) has a long cylindrical spike of cream flowers. Sheep's-bit has flat heads of tiny star-shaped flowers and no horns. Devil's-bit scabious has opposite leaves and a fuzzy dome.
